title: How do we multiply an Egyptian numeral by ten?
description: A numeral with a coil, two heels and a stroke is multiplied by ten, one symbol at a time, using the distributive property. The pattern is then used on a second numeral. Keeko's doubt is that only the biggest symbol moves up.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying by ten moves every symbol up one landmark, because each part is multiplied by ten. Watch for students who move only the biggest symbol and leave the rest.

source: Multiply 121 (1 coil, 2 heels, 1 stroke) by 10, then use the rule to find 522 × 10.
video_script.why: The child multiplies an Egyptian numeral by ten using the distributive property and finds the rule that every symbol moves up one landmark.
video_script.substitution: Split the numeral into its landmarks, multiply each one by ten, and add the results.
video_script.anchor: the book's numeral of one coil, two heels and one stroke, multiplied by ten
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko moves only the coil to a lotus and leaves the heels and the stroke; the numeral then reads 1021, which is too small
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred twenty one times ten is one thousand two hundred ten.

final_answer.value: 121 × 10 is 1210 (1 lotus, 2 coils, 1 heel) and 522 × 10 is 5220
final_answer.spoken: one hundred twenty one times ten is one thousand two hundred ten, and five hundred twenty two times ten is five thousand two hundred twenty

hold_back: 121 × 10 is 1210 (1 lotus, 2 coils, 1 heel) and 522 × 10 is 5220
maths_rules: (100 + 10 + 10 + 1) x 10 = 100 x 10 + 10 x 10 + 10 x 10 + 1 x 10 (distributive property)
522 = 500 + 20 + 2 = 5 coils, 2 heels, 2 strokes; times 10: 5 lotuses, 2 coils, 2 heels = 5000 + 200 + 20 = 5220
Keeko's slip: moving only the coil gives 1 lotus, 2 heels, 1 stroke = 1000 + 20 + 1 = 1021
video_script.design: One idea: every symbol moves up one landmark. The numeral stays on the board; each symbol shows an arrow up to its new symbol.

<bookmark mark='sym'/>Here is a numeral with one coil, two heels and one stroke.

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>A landmark times ten is the next landmark. A stroke becomes a heel, a heel becomes a coil, and a coil becomes a lotus.
<bookmark mark='dist'/>The distributive property also works with more than two parts. A sum times ten is each part times ten, added.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to multiply it by ten, and then use the pattern for five hundred twenty two.

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, split the numeral into its landmarks. A coil, two heels and a stroke are one hundred, ten, ten and one.
<bookmark mark='times'/>We multiply the whole sum by ten.

marks.dist: each part is multiplied by 10 separately
marks.vals: the four results 1000, 100, 100 and 10 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='dist'/>Step two, use the distributive property. Multiply each part by ten on its own.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>One hundred times ten is one thousand. Ten times ten is one hundred, twice, and one times ten is ten.

beats.on_screen: 1000 + 100 + 100 + 10 = 1210 = 1 lotus, 2 coils, 1 heel; every symbol moved up one landmark

marks.up: each symbol moves up one landmark: the coil to a lotus, the heels to coils, the stroke to a heel

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the four parts. We get one thousand two hundred ten, which is a lotus, two coils and a heel.
<bookmark mark='up'/>Look at the symbols. The coil became a lotus, the two heels became coils, and the stroke became a heel.

narration: <bookmark mark='num'/>Step four, use the pattern for five hundred twenty two. It is five coils, two heels and two strokes.
<bookmark mark='up'/>Move every symbol up one landmark. We get five lotuses, two coils and two heels.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check by value. Five thousand plus two hundred plus twenty is five thousand two hundred twenty.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only the coil moves up, so the heels and the stroke stay as they are.
<bookmark mark='read'/>That numeral reads one thousand twenty one, which is far too small.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Every part is multiplied by ten, so every symbol must move up one landmark.
